title: Serre H1 vanishing on polynomial Proj
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P=\operatorname{Proj} k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $G$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_P$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. With $\mathcal O_P(d)=\mathrm{Proj.twist}(d)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], there exists $b\in\mathbf Z$ such that for every integer $d\ge b$, $H^1(P,G\otimes\mathcal O_P(d))=0$. Cohomology is sheaf cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology], represented in Lean by Scheme.Modules.H.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 01YS (4), Tag 01MN (1),(2); proof step 2 of lem-sc-p1-section-coordinate-surjective

proof.text: Use proj_shifted_free_is_twist k 0 only to obtain the chart-compatible scheme isomorphism C from polynomial Proj to the relative projective line. No finite-coproduct or fraction data is needed.

Derive finite presentation from coherence without a Noetherian hypothesis. Choose finite local generators and reindex their finite index sets by ULift(Fin n). The coherence kernel clause gives finite-type relations. Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentFiniteTypeLocallyNoetherian and apply its existing private isFinitePresentation_of_generators_kernel theorem on each slice site. Descend these local finite presentations using IsFinitePresentation.of_coversTop. Mathlib supplies quasi-coherence from finite presentation. The only local helper carries out reindexing and cover descent; the finite-generator/kernel construction is reused rather than duplicated.

The isomorphism C.iso.hom is a closed immersion. Apply the closed-immersion form of Serre theorem B, Scheme.Modules.exists_subsingleton_H_tensor_twist, to G. It gives one integer b for all sufficiently large twists and all positive cohomological degrees; specialize to degree one. This theorem is the existing Serre-module wrapper around projective-space Serre vanishing and its pushforward/cohomology comparison.

For each integer d use proj_twist_inverse_transport k C d. Pull its isomorphism back by C.iso.hom, and cancel the composite of C.iso.hom and C.iso.inv using pullbackComp, pullbackCongr and pullbackId. This identifies the polynomial Proj twist with the pullback of the relative projective-space twist. Tensor its inverse with the identity of G; subsingleton_H_of_iso transports the degree-one vanishing supplied in the previous step to G tensor Proj.twist d. No positivity assumption on d is required for the comparison.

theorem exists_subsingleton_H_one_tensor_proj_twist
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).Modules)
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent

      Subsingleton ((G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) d).H 1)
